content.comment_body: Regarding the two output terminals, does the wiring order matter? The manual states that +24V should be connected to the right terminal and the load to the left terminal before going to neutral. I have connected +24V to the left terminal and my load to the right terminal, then to neutral. Could this cause issues? My output does not deactivate as expected, even though the program works in simulation, so I suspect a hardware problem. Any suggestions would be appreciated.
It would be helpful if you specify which type of device you are using.
I'm using a pure 24V base module: Part No. [article_no], Type [article_no].

That's the order number of a complete unit. If I'm correct, it includes a relay module with clock functionality. In that case, the way the outputs are connected does not affect functionality. On your operator device in the box, you can check if the output is active. Note that working in simulation does not guarantee the same behavior in the actual device. Try a simple program connecting input directly to output and test again.

I've identified the issue—it was a programming problem. I used the F1 button on the operator panel as an on/off switch and must have activated it twice, which caused the output Q1 to remain energized. If I hadn’t pressed it twice, the F1 button might not have latched, even though it was configured as a switch. In my urgency to set up the new control box, I overlooked this. I've attached my program for reference in case someone else faces a similar issue. Thanks for your feedback.
Function keys on the device work like standard digital inputs. The switch setting is only meant for simulation, not for physical operation on the actual device.

analysis.insight_summary: Users experienced uncertainty regarding correct wiring for output terminals on the [product_name] device. Initial concerns about hardware malfunction were later found to be related to program logic and interaction with the function key (F1) on the operator panel. The issue highlighted differences between simulation and the real device, especially in input key behavior and troubleshooting approaches.
analysis.user_expectations: Users seek clear, reliable wiring instructions, accurate simulation that reflects real device operation, and transparent feedback from input keys and outputs.
